To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) monocyte-derived macrophages are required to limit local tissue damage following dermal infection with virulent poxvirus; 2) a systemic response is required to control the spread of virus to the systemic compartment; and 3) the subcapsular macrophages of draining lymph nodes are not required for systemic control.

1) monocyte populations recruited early after dermal infection of VACV are important for control of local pathogenicity but are dispensable to prevent systemic spread; 2) subcapsular sinus cells are dispensable to contain VACV spread; 3) systemic macrophage depletion allows VACV to spread to the spleen; 4) the function of macrophages but not dendritic cell is required to prevent VACV spread to the liver and brain;
systemic depletion of macrophages, and not dendritic cells (DCs) or neutrophils, allows VACV to disseminate from the site of infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which the innate immune system prevents systemic dissemination of a virus following a peripheral infection.
the innate immune response that occurs at the site of infection and in the draining lymph node following a peripheral infection.
the innate immune response to a viral infection at a peripheral tissue site and the role of the draining lymph nodes and systemic macrophages in preventing systemic spread of the virus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
systemic depletion of macrophages, not subcapsular sinus cells, is required for systemic spread of virus.
systemic macrophages play an important role in preventing dissemination of VACV, but the role of the subcapsular macrophages in preventing spread is not as critical as was previously suggested.
the innate immune response, particularly macrophages, play a critical role during the early stages of a viral infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the innate immune response is not a simple linear process.
a systemic macrophage mediated innate response is required to prevent systemic infection and pathology following a peripheral infection with a poxvirus.
a systemic macrophage population is required to prevent systemic dissemination of virus following infection with VACV at the skin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune response to a peripheral viral infection is a systemic response.
the systemic immune system plays a role in preventing spread of a virus from the site of inoculation.
a systemic macrophage population is required to prevent systemic infection following a peripheral infection.
